specification:
Write a valid COBOL program that updates a master file with transaction data. The program should:

- Follow the standard COBOL division structure (IDENTIFICATION, ENVIRONMENT, DATA, and PROCEDURE divisions) 
- Adhere to COBOL Area A and Area B coding conventions
- Use standard COBOL indentation, especially in PROCEDURE DIVISION, to improve readability

The program will read an old master file (task_func35_inp1) and a transaction file (task_func35_inp2). For each record, it should:

- If the account numbers match, add the transaction amount to the master record amount and write the updated record to a new master file (task_func35_out)
- If only the master record exists, write it to the new master file unchanged  
- If only the transaction record exists, write a new record with the transaction data to the new master file

At the end, close all files. The records use the following format:

Master:  05 account-no PIC X(5), 05 amount PIC 9(4)V99. 
Transaction: 05 account-no PIC X(5), 05 amount PIC 9(4)V99.
Output: 05 account-no PIC X(5), 05 amount PIC 9(5)V99.

Ensure the program handles reaching the end of either input file gracefully. The output file should contain the updated master records in account number order.
